title: Numerical differentiation and integration
subtitle: Slopes from differences, areas from slices — and how error shrinks as the slices get thinner.

diff.title: Numerical differentiation
diff.body: From the definition f′(x) ≈ [f(x + h) − f(x)]/h (forward difference, error O(h)); the central difference [f(x + h) − f(x − h)]/(2h) has error O(h²). Shrinking h reduces truncation error but amplifies round-off error, so there is an optimal h (around 10⁻⁵ for double precision central differences).
diff.steps: Estimate the derivative of sin x at x = 0 with h = 0.1. Central: [sin 0.1 − sin(−0.1)]/0.2 = 0.19967/0.2. Forward: sin 0.1 / 0.1 = 0.99833 too at this point (symmetry); at other x the central is much better.

trap.title: The trapezoidal rule
trap.body: Replace the curve over each subinterval by a straight line: ∫f ≈ h[½f₀ + f₁ + … + fn−1 + ½fₙ]. The error is O(h²) — halve h, quarter the error. For ∫₀^π sin x dx = 2: four intervals give 1.896119 (error 1.04e-1); 32 intervals give 1.998393.
trap.steps: n = 4 strips on [0, π]: h = π/4 and the function values at 0, π/4, π/2, 3π/4, π. Trapezoid sum.

simp.title: Simpson’s rule
simp.body: Fit a parabola through each pair of strips: ∫f ≈ (h/3)[f₀ + 4f₁ + 2f₂ + 4f₃ + … + fₙ], with n even. The error is O(h⁴) and the rule is exact for cubics. Same four intervals: Simpson gives 2.00456 (error 4.56e-3) — much better than the trapezoid's 1.04e-1.
simp.steps: n = 4, h = π/4; coefficients 1, 4, 2, 4, 1 on the values 0, .7071, 1, .7071, 0. Sum.

romberg.title: Richardson extrapolation and Romberg
romberg.body: If the trapezoid error is C·h², then from estimates T(h) and T(h/2): better = [4T(h/2) − T(h)]/3 cancels the h² term. Repeating gives Romberg integration, a triangle of ever better values. Note that one extrapolation of the trapezoid rule equals Simpson's rule.

gauss.title: Gauss quadrature (idea)
gauss.body: Newton–Cotes rules fix equally spaced nodes. Gaussian quadrature chooses both nodes and weights: an n-point rule is exact for polynomials up to degree 2n − 1. The two-point rule on [−1, 1] uses nodes ±1/√3 with weights 1 and 1.
gauss.steps: Integrate x² on [−1, 1] by the 2-point Gauss rule. = 2/3, the exact value.

summary.title: Summary
summary.body:
• Central difference O(h²); trapezoid O(h²); Simpson O(h⁴), n even.
  • Extrapolate to cancel leading error terms.
